tagline: Across the San Jacinto Valley, past an old polar landing.
intro: The Ramona Expressway crosses the San Jacinto Valley from the Lake Perris country to San Jacinto. Along the way it passes Lakeview, then comes into a city that was laid out at Five Points in 1883 and incorporated the year the railroad arrived, 1888.

Agriculture and dairies built the local economy, and tourists came for the nearby hot springs. The valley is also where Helen Hunt Jackson set her story Ramona, written after she visited in the 1880s, and San Jacinto helped start the Ramona Pageant in 1923.

moments.title: Lakeview
moments.text: Named for nearby Mystic Lake, the community stands on the old Rancho San Jacinto Nuevo y Potrero, an 1846 Mexican land grant that also took in the site of Lake Perris.

moments.title: Gromov flight marker, San Jacinto
moments.text: A stone marker on Cottonwood Avenue recalls July 15, 1937, when Mikhail Gromov's crew of three ended a 6,262-mile polar flight from Moscow in San Jacinto.

moments.title: Valle Vista
moments.text: Bautista Creek, whose canyon Juan Bautista de Anza passed through in 1774 and 1776, comes down channelized and joins the San Jacinto River just north of town.
